questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Discipline and Its Name' refers to.
questions.a: Human Ecology and Family Sciences studies the individual and the family within their total ecology -- home, community, resources and environment. The name itself signals the discipline's evolution from narrow household arts to a science of interdependence between people and their surroundings.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Discipline and Its Name'.
questions.a: The subject studies people not alone but nested in family, community and environment -- an ecology of daily life.

concepts.title: Concerns of the Discipline: Adolescence, Family and Resources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Concerns of the Discipline: Adolescence, Family and Resources' refers to.
questions.a: The course is organised around life stages and living concerns: understanding oneself in adolescence, food and health, management of resources, fabrics and apparel, media and communication, and the growth of family, community and society through childhood into adulthood.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Concerns of the Discipline: Adolescence, Family and Resources'.
questions.a: From self to family to society -- the discipline walks the learner through life's stages and material world.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Concerns of the Discipline: Adolescence, Family and Resources' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Relevance to Quality of Life and Careers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Relevance to Quality of Life and Careers' refers to.
questions.a: The discipline matters because its questions are everyone's questions -- eating well, dressing suitably, spending wisely, growing healthy children and maintaining relationships. Its knowledge opens careers in nutrition, counselling, textiles, resource management and community work, serving both self and society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Relevance to Quality of Life and Careers'.
questions.a: A subject of everyday life -- and therefore a springboard to professions that serve everyday life.
